entities.summary: Johann Christoph Friedrich Klug, was a German entomologist. He described the butterflies and some other insects of Upper Egypt and Arabia in Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg and Wilhelm Friedrich Hemprich's Symbolæ Physicæ. He was professor of medicine and entomology in the University of Berlin where he curated the insect collections from 1810 to 1856. At the same time he directed the Botanic Garden in Berlin which contains his collections. Klug worked mainly on Hymenoptera and Coleoptera. The plant genus Klugia was named in his honour as well as the butterflies Geitoneura klugii and Heliophisma klugii.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Klug's work on Hymenoptera and Coleoptera contributed significantly to entomology, with his collections at the University of Berlin serving as a valuable resource for future researchers. The plant genus Klugia and butterfly species named in his honor reflect his lasting impact on the field.
